raw_text:
Fourth review of run r-20260921T053228459971-node-probe (plan imas-ambix:serve-telemetry-spine
section 3), read at its fourth-round head b9bbdeb0 on base 39e7bba5. The third review, at
dcf458dc, scored 94 and reported one defect: the timeout assertion keyed its recorded calls by
argv[0], so the two cat reads shared one key and the /proc/stat read's bound was asserted by
nothing. The repair of that defect, 65bf2443, is what this record reads, so this is the fourth
look and it re-scores the landed change. Read at b9bbdeb0: imas_ambix/agent/node_probe.py (579
lines, sha256 f78e35a99445dbf316203befc403856d499ed9d43cbeab706a70757f3dc4ca4f, byte-identical to
dcf458dc) and tests/test_node_probe.py (519 lines, sha256
dbb7e61c19ede9daf03edd4c7b7b96e578ba0f53eea399a470fdd67d1fa296e9, up from 486), the two
commits, the plan section, the landing record and the four control artifacts in the run
directory. Every check below was run in this reviewer's own scratch copy of the two files, in
the repository's shared project environment (pytest 9.1.1, Python 3.14.2); nothing here was run
on a GPU node or against a live serve.

VERDICT goal: the round's goal is that each of the four reads' declared bound be the bound it is
actually invoked with, and be asserted as such; all four are pinned at b9bbdeb0 -- displacing the
cards bound at node_probe.py:274, the /proc/stat bound at :431, the /proc/meminfo bound at :439 or
the squeue bound at :516, one at a time and 0.25 s each, fails three assertions in every case (3
failed, 31 passed, four logs in the scratch directory) against a baseline of 34 passed, where the
same displacement of the /proc/stat bound was the green case the third review measured.
VERDICT done_when: the dispatched measure is this parsed record; the node's own measure was the
re-keying with its control, re-derived here as 34 passed at b9bbdeb0 and ruff --no-cache exiting 0
over both files, and the control replayed to the red its own log records.
VERDICT write_paths: 65bf2443 touches tests/test_node_probe.py alone and b9bbdeb0 touches
docs/plans/serve-telemetry-spine.html and docs/evidence/archive/serve-telemetry-spine-landed.html
alone, all inside the node's declared paths, with serving_receipts.py untouched as plan section 7's
build/wire split requires.
VERDICT manifest: read; it names the fourth defect and its repair, carries the control under
negative_control_log_cpu_bound and states the control's two runs, both of which were replayed here
and both of which reproduced -- but its after_suite sentence still dates the whole-tree lint to
dcf458dc, an older head than the lint log beside it, so that label trails the round it describes.
VERDICT diff: read commit by commit; 65bf2443 rewrites the recording runner to key both its calls
and its responses by the whole argument vector, answers each cat read with its own body rather than
answering both from one, asserts each of the four vectors separately and adds a count check of the
mapping against the recorded call list so a collision fails loudly; b9bbdeb0 records the finding,
the re-keying and the pair of control runs on the landing record and on the plan comment.

SCORE goal_fidelity: 20
JUSTIFICATION goal_fidelity: node_probe.py:558/562/563/571 pass the probe's own bounds to the four
reads and each single-read displacement of node_probe.py:274/431/439/516 is red in this reviewer's
run, so the figure each read is invoked with is the figure asserted.
SCORE evidence: 18
JUSTIFICATION evidence: the control's declared text was replayed through the run's own plugin
(mutate_cpu_bound.py) and reproduced 3 failed, 31 passed exactly, and against the test file at the
previous head (dcf458dc, sha 9e390ff46a8de6748a45799cb89ef7ce5f39a8882a93bfe07b5c117859a9f457, 486
lines) reproduced 1 failed, 33 passed with only the positional test red, which is the finding the
record claims; docked for the residuals the record itself discloses (the card body is a
recorded-shape fixture rather than a capture, and section 3's under-one-percent-of-one-core clause
remains unmeasured).
SCORE scope_discipline: 20
JUSTIFICATION scope_discipline: the two commits touch the test file and the two documents alone and
nothing else in the declared range, and no path outside the node's declared write paths appears in
either.
SCORE durability: 17
JUSTIFICATION durability: the four bounds are now pinned (four single-read mutations red, measured)
and the new collapse guard fires with "two reads collapsed onto one vector" at
tests/test_node_probe.py:487 and tests/test_node_probe.py:507 when the two cat reads are handed one
vector (measured, --tb=line log), but the card query's field strings remain pinned by nothing
(finding below) and the command-keyed response mappings at tests/test_node_probe.py:429/434 and
:142 are the same shape left in place, inert today, shown so by measurement.
SCORE fit: 19
JUSTIFICATION fit: the re-keying keeps the file's idiom -- a declared figure being the one in force,
stated in the docstring at tests/test_node_probe.py:470-477 -- the two files are clean on all five
naming scans with the two benign hits read and kept, and ruff --no-cache exits 0 over both.

FINDING tests/test_node_probe.py:113 the expected card-query vector is derived from
node_probe.CARD_QUERY_FIELDS, the same constant the module queries with, so the expectation moves
with the mutation it should catch: replacing "power.draw" with "power.watts" in CARD_FIELDS at
node_probe.py:64 leaves the suite at 34 passed (measured, one-sample run in this reviewer's
scratch copy), while the literal part of the same tuple is pinned -- changing
"--format=csv,noheader,nounits" at node_probe.py:272 fails two tests. On a node a field the driver
does not accept makes nvidia-smi exit non-zero, run_capture returns None and the cards section is
silently absent from every row -- the module's own designed absence, indistinguishable from a
card-less node, so nothing would report it.

SETTLED SUSPICIONS -- the four remaining argv[0] sites named in the dispatch:
tests/test_node_probe.py:86 responses.get(argv[0]): the collapse cannot apply, because no assertion
resting on this mapping needs the two cat reads told apart -- the mapping is used for the cards and
the job table (distinct commands, one read each) and, at tests/test_node_probe.py:407, for an
all-None probe whose assertion is that nothing is reported at all. The pair is discriminated by
_host_runner (tests/test_node_probe.py:100-107, dispatching on argv[1]) and by the vector-keyed
recording, which is why dropping the meminfo read from the tick is red (2 failed via the count
assertion, measured).
tests/test_node_probe.py:100 if argv[0] != "cat": this is a dispatch on the command followed by a
dispatch on the path, inverts to None for any path that is neither path. It cannot collapse:
reading a path swap through it yields the wrong body and the assertions go red.
tests/test_node_probe.py:429 and :434: this IS the fixed defect's shape left in place -- a mapping
keyed by the command with both cat reads behind the single "cat" key and one stat body answering
both -- but no assertion in that test distinguishes them (it asserts section presence per tick and
calls.count("squeue") == 2, and the meminfo read's answer parses to no memory fields, so the host
section there is cpu-only). I could not construct an input that hides behind it: giving read_meminfo
the /proc/stat vector at node_probe.py:439 is caught by the host tests and by the count assertion
(4 failed, measured), and dropping the meminfo call is caught by the recording tests' count
assertion at tests/test_node_probe.py:463 and :485 (2 failed, measured). Same shape, inert today --
reported as a follow-on, not a finding, because no concrete input breaks it.
tests/test_node_probe.py:142 the recording runner's squeue branch is also keyed by the command
rather than by the whole vector, but there is one squeue read, its vector is asserted verbatim at
tests/test_node_probe.py:349-350, and a wrong vector is caught by the mapping lookup in the two
bound tests, so two distinct reads cannot share the key.

NAMING SCAN, both files at b9bbdeb0: paths, banned label words, bare deliverable ids, changelog
prose and attribution all clean; the two hits read and kept are node_probe.py:533 "records an old
measurement as a current one", which is prose about staleness rather than a version suffix, and the
captured job name "deepseek-v4-1-flash" at tests/test_node_probe.py:71/323, which is fixture data.
